title: Sum of nine marked angles
statement: Inside △ABC, nine marked angles a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i are grouped as the complete angle sets of three triangles: (a,g,f), (b,i,c), (d,e,h). Find a+b+c+d+e+f+g+h+i.
local_hints: The requested nine angles already form three complete triangle angle-sets.

title: Angle bisectors in a parallelogram
statement: In parallelogram ABCD, the bisector of ∠DAB meets BC at M. The bisector of ∠AMC passes through D. Given ∠MDC=45°, find the smaller interior angle of the parallelogram.
local_hints: Mark both bisected angles before introducing variables.
Recall GEO-PAR-01 · Transfer angles through parallels.

title: Equilateral triangle inside an isosceles triangle
statement: In isosceles △ABC with AB=AC, an equilateral △DEF is inscribed with D∈AB, E∈AC, F∈BC. Define a=∠BFD, b=∠ADE, c=∠FEC. Determine the relation among a,b,c.
local_hints: Use the outer isosceles triangle and the inner 60° angles together.
Recall GEO-ISO-01 · Turn equal lengths into equal angles.

title: Extended sides of a regular polygon
statement: Two sides of a regular n-gon, when extended, meet at an angle of 28°. What is the smallest possible n?
local_hints: Extended sides are lines, so their directions are compared modulo 180°.
Recall GEO-POLY-01 · Think in exterior turns.
If k side-turns separate the directions, write k·360°/n ≡ ±28° (mod 180°) and seek the smallest n.

title: Rectangle cut into four triangles
statement: Rectangle ABCD has E on CD and F on BC. Given [ADE]=16, [CEF]=9, [ABF]=25, find [AEF].
local_hints: Treat 16, 9, and 25 as three pieces of one unknown rectangle area.
Recall GEO-AREA-01 · Solve the whole area before chasing pieces.

title: A reflection creates an equilateral triangle
statement: In isosceles △ABC, AB=AC and ∠BAC=99.4°. Point D satisfies AD=DB and ∠BAD=19.7°. Compute ∠BDC.
local_hints: AD=DB gives an isosceles triangle; the angle data hides a 60° construction.
Recall GEO-TRANS-01 · Use reflection to manufacture structure.
First mark the equal base angles from AD=DB; then look for a reflection that turns the remaining 60° gap into an equilateral triangle.

title: Diameter and intersecting lines
statement: A circle has centre C. Q and S lie on the circle, QC is extended through C to the opposite point P. Line PR meets CS at A and QS at B. Given ∠QPR=24° and ∠CAP=90°, find ∠QBR.
local_hints: P,C,Q are collinear, and ∠CAP=90° makes triangle CAP the clean starting point.
Recall GEO-RIGHT-01 · Exploit right-triangle structure first.

title: Central angles and an equilateral triangle
statement: A,B,D,E lie on a circle with centre C. If ∠BCD=72° and CD=DE, determine ∠BAE.
local_hints: CD=CE because both are radii, and CD=DE is also given.

title: Hidden SAS congruence
statement: B,D,C are collinear with D between B and C. AC=AE, AB=AD, and ∠BAD=∠EAC. If BD=10 and DC=4, find DE.
local_hints: The given equal angle is only part of the included angle needed for SAS.

title: Ratio of diagonal segments in a cyclic quadrilateral
statement: A,B,C,D lie on a circle in that order with AB=3, BC=5, CD=6, DA=4. Diagonals AC and BD meet at P. Compute AP/CP.
local_hints: The intersecting diagonals create two AA-similar pairs from same-chord angles.
Recall GEO-CIRCLE-01 · Track the chord or arc, then GEO-SIM-01.

title: Orthocenter and incenter on one circle
statement: In △ABC, H,I,O are the orthocenter, incenter, and circumcenter. If B,H,I,C are concyclic, find ∠BOC.
local_hints: Write the standard angles ∠BHC and ∠BIC in terms of ∠A.
Recall GEO-CENTER-01 · Identify triangle centres from their defining lines.

title: Perpendicular medians
statement: In △ABC, the median from B is perpendicular to the median from C. The median from A has length 30. Determine (BC²+CA²+AB²)/100.
local_hints: The perpendicular medians meet at the centroid, where the 2:1 ratio is usable.
Recall GEO-MEDIAN-01 · Classify medians and use the centroid.
Place the centroid at the origin; then a+b+c=0 and perpendicular median directions give a dot-product relation.

title: Orthocenter of the pedal triangle on a diameter circle
statement: ABC is acute. The circle Γ with BC as diameter meets AB and AC again at P and Q. Determine ∠BAC if the orthocenter of △APQ lies on Γ.
local_hints: The circle with BC as diameter turns P and Q into right-angle feet.
Use Thales first: CP⊥AB and BQ⊥AC. Express the orthocenter of △APQ using those altitude directions before imposing that it lies on Γ.
